evidence: src/domain/order-state.ts defines NEXT_STATE, CANCELLABLE, nextStateOf, isCancellable as the single source of lifecycle rules
src/domain/order.ts Order.advance()/cancel() delegate to nextStateOf/isCancellable rather than redefining transitions
src/domain/product.ts Product.canReserve(quantity) holds the stock-availability invariant; Product.reserve uses it
src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts StockReservationService.reserve pre-checks via product.canReserve and mutates via product.reserve, going through ProductRepository
src/domain/errors.ts DomainError base with ValidationError, NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError, InvalidStateTransitionError used consistently across the module
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The domain module covers one concern: order fulfilment, meaning orders, their lifecycle, product stock and the repository and ID-generator interfaces, plus shared domain errors. Order lifecycle rules live only in order-state.ts (NEXT_STATE, CANCELLABLE, nextStateOf, isCancellable), and Order uses those helpers instead of redefining them. The stock rule (quantity <= available) is defined once in Product.canReserve. StockReservationService calls canReserve first so it can reserve all items or none, then calls Product.reserve, so it does not bypass or copy the rule. Only the error message text is repeated, not the rule. Quantity checks are split by meaning: OrderItem requires a positive whole number, Product requires a starting stock of zero or more. All errors extend DomainError. No file splits off into an unrelated concern or goes around the module's own abstractions.
